previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted at the direction of his hepatologist due to worsening fatigue, hyponatremia, and anemia. He had no signs of infection or active bleeding. A diagnostic paracentesis showed no evidence of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis. He received one unit of packed red blood cells and two days of albumin infusion to address anemia and low sodium. His TIPS shunt remained patent but showed increased mid-shunt velocities on Doppler ultrasound, warranting outpatient follow-up imaging. Diuretics were held due to refractory hyponatremia, and lactulose was increased to 30 mL three times daily due to trace asterixis. He was discharged home in stable condition with plans for primary care and hepatology follow-up, repeat TIPS ultrasound, and close monitoring for changes in weight, mental status, or abdominal girth.
